opex.name: Operating & SG&A
opex.note: Running the stores, the supply chain and the back office — 21.2% of revenue.

flow.otherDetail: Interest, net of $685M, plus a $341M net loss on equity and other investments.

follow100Note: Kept-as-profit is the $4,945M attributable to Walmart shareholders; consolidated net income was $5,095M before the $150M noncontrolling share. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Net profit here is the $4,945M attributable to Walmart shareholders (EPS $0.62); consolidated net income was $5,095M before $150M attributable to noncontrolling interests. Walmart reports gross profit as net sales minus cost of sales ($45,754M); this page's gross profit ($47,832M) adds the $2,078M of membership and other income so the flow starts from total revenue.
oneTimers: A $341M net loss on equity and other investments sits below operating income, vs a $2,081M gain a year ago — a $2.4B swing. Adjusted EPS of $0.65 excludes this $0.03-per-share drag. These are mark-to-market moves on Walmart's strategic stakes, not store operations.

Last year's International operating income carried a $722M non-cash share-based compensation charge at PhonePe (share plans modified ahead of a potential IPO), which makes this quarter's +132.6% International operating-income growth look far stronger than the underlying +7.0% adjusted constant-currency growth.
Last year's quarter also included a $155M reversal of a previously accrued legal charge in Corporate and support; there is no equivalent adjustment this quarter.
Flipkart's Big Billion Days sale shifted into Q4, costing International about 500 bps of net-sales growth this quarter; the offsetting benefit is expected in Q4 FY27.
pngFooterNote: Gross profit here includes $2.1B membership income.

segments.name: Walmart U.S.
segments.note: The big U.S. stores — net sales up 3.6%, comparable sales up 2.9%, eCommerce up 23%, and operating income up 9.0% to $6.3B.

segments.name: Walmart International
segments.note: Stores and e-commerce outside the U.S., including Flipkart in India — net sales up 7.0%, operating income $1.6B, though the jump is flattered by lapping last year's $0.7B PhonePe charge.

segments.name: Sam's Club U.S.
segments.note: The warehouse-club business — net sales up 10.0% and eCommerce up 30%, but operating income fell 15.8% to $547M on lapped breakage income, a LIFO charge, and the new bundled membership.

segments.name: Membership & other income
segments.note: Walmart+ and Sam's Club membership fees plus rent and other income — membership fee revenue grew 17% globally.

takeaways.text: Operating income rose 16.0% to $7.8B (5.5% on an adjusted constant-currency basis) and Walmart raised full-year guidance. Net income fell only because of the investment swing below the operating line — judge this quarter on operating income, not EPS.
takeaways.title: The stores earned more — the headline didn't show it

takeaways.text: Walmart booked a $341M net loss on its equity and other investments this quarter, vs a $2,081M gain a year ago. Adjusted EPS, which strips that out, actually grew 4.8%, to $0.65 from $0.62.
takeaways.title: A $2.4B swing in investments explains the profit drop

takeaways.text: Global eCommerce sales grew 17% (U.S. +23%), global advertising 25% (U.S. +37%), and membership fees 17%. Guidance raised for FY27: net sales +4.9–5.2% and adjusted operating income +8.0–8.6% in constant currency, adjusted EPS $2.84–$2.89.
takeaways.title: eCommerce and advertising are the growth engine

verdict: Walmart's sales grew 5.2% to $188.8B and operating profit rose 16% as eCommerce jumped 17% — but headline profit fell 19.5% because last year's quarter included a $2.1B gain on investments that flipped to a $0.3B loss.
